title: Arise, O LORD, to Your Resting Place

verses.text: O LORD, remember on behalf of David all the hardships he endured,
how he swore an oath to the LORD, and vowed to the Mighty One of Jacob:
"I will not enter my house or get into my bed,
I will not give sleep to my eyes or slumber to my eyelids,
until I find a place for the LORD, a dwelling for the Mighty One of Jacob."
We heard that the ark was in Ephrathah; we found it in the fields of Jaar.
Let us go to His dwelling place; let us worship at His footstool.
Arise, O LORD, to Your resting place, You and the ark of Your strength.
May Your priests be clothed with righteousness, and Your saints shout for joy.
For the sake of Your servant David, do not reject Your anointed one.
The LORD swore an oath to David, a promise He will not revoke: "One of your descendants I will place on your throne.
If your sons keep My covenant and the testimony I will teach them, then their sons will also sit on your throne forever and ever."
For the LORD has chosen Zion; He has desired it for His home:
"This is My resting place forever and ever; here I will dwell, for I have desired this home.
I will bless her with abundant provisions; I will satisfy her poor with bread.
I will clothe her priests with salvation, and her saints will sing out in joy.
There I will make a horn grow for David; I have prepared a lamp for My anointed one.
I will clothe his enemies with shame, but the crown upon him will gleam."

context.author: The title calls it “A song of ascents,” one of fifteen such psalms (120-134). They may have been sung by pilgrims going up to Jerusalem for the feasts; the Mishnah says the Levites sang them on the fifteen steps inside the Temple courts (Sukkah 5:4).
context.genre: Psalm: a song or prayer in Hebrew poetry
context.audience: Israel at worship, and the nations called to join
context.mapLabel: FROM THE FIELDS OF JAAR TO ZION
context.setting: “O LORD, remember on behalf of David all the hardships he endured” (v.1), and his oath not to rest “until I find a place for the LORD, a dwelling for the Mighty One of Jacob” (v.5). The people remember finding the ark: “We heard that the ark was in Ephrathah; we found it in the fields of Jaar” (v.6). “Let us go to His dwelling place; let us worship at His footstool. Arise, O LORD, to Your resting place, You and the ark of Your strength” (vv.7-8). Then God’s own oath to David: “One of your descendants I will place on your throne” (v.11). “For the LORD has chosen Zion… ‘This is My resting place forever and ever; here I will dwell’” (vv.13-14). He will bless her, clothe her priests with salvation, and “There I will make a horn grow for David; I have prepared a lamp for My anointed one” (v.17).
context.custom: After the Philistines returned the ark, it stayed for twenty years at Kiriath-jearim, ‘the town of the forests,’ here called the fields of Jaar (1 Samuel 7:1-2), until David brought it to Jerusalem (2 Samuel 6). Ephrathah is an old name for the Bethlehem area (Micah 5:2). A horn stands for strength, and a lamp for a dynasty that does not go out (1 Kings 11:36).
context.timelineImmediate: Psalm 133: how good and pleasant it is when brothers live together in harmony.
context.timelineBible: Solomon ended his prayer at the Temple’s dedication with vv.8-10 (2 Chronicles 6:41-42). Peter said David knew “that God had promised him on oath that He would place one of his descendants on his throne” (Acts 2:30). Zechariah praised God for raising up “a horn of salvation for us in the house of His servant David” (Luke 1:69).

gospelParallels.note: A horn of salvation in the house of David.

otBackground.note: David brings the ark to Zion.
Arise, O LORD, to Your resting place.

overview.summary: Pilgrims remember David’s oath to find a home for the ark and God’s oath to David: He has chosen Zion as His resting place forever and will raise a horn for David’s line.

archaeology.t: Recent digs at Tel Qiryat Yearim found a large raised platform from the 8th century BC.
The Psalms Scroll from Qumran preserves this psalm with the Songs of Ascents.

overview.discussion: David would not rest until God had a dwelling (vv.3-5). What place does God have at the center of my life?
overview.book: The book of Psalms · 150 psalms (all 150 in the app). Israel’s songs and prayers: praise, lament, thanks, trust and wisdom, many of them by David.
overview.author: Not named
